policy: Batches 1-3 of the 2000-ly nebula census. Reflection nebulae, H II regions and planetary nebulae at least 5 arcmin across whose adopted distance minus its error is within 613.2 pc (2000 ly). Distances prefer the SIMBAD-adopted parallax of the illuminating or central star; cluster parallaxes or VLBA parallaxes replace stars whose own parallax is unreliable or embedded. Positions and identifiers come from SIMBAD (CfA mirror, retrieved 2026-11-03). Sizes come from Sharpless (1959) for H II regions, Lynds (1965) for NGC/IC nebulae, twice the van den Bergh (1966) maximum radius otherwise, the SIMBAD-adopted angular diameter or HASH radius for planetary nebulae, and ESO/Uppsala or van den Bergh & Herbst (1975) south of the Lynds limit. Batch 4 adds the supernova remnants within 2000 ly whose distances are established: the Vela Supernova Remnant, the Monogem Ring and Hoinga. Their shells are modeled from published centers, sizes and distances, because the H-alpha map cannot trace them. Batch 5 adds the Crab Nebula beyond the cutoff as a showcase, at the VLBI parallax distance of its pulsar, with its filaments from the published 3D map of Martin, Milisavljevic & Drissen (2021).

deferred.barnards-loop: Published distances disagree (about 170 pc against about 440 pc); a 10-degree arc needs a settled distance.
deferred.ngc-1788: Lynds (1965) lists 2 x 2 arcmin, below the 5-arcmin census limit.
deferred.ngc-246: 3.7 arcmin SIMBAD-adopted diameter, below the 5-arcmin census limit.
deferred.m43: Inside the 65 x 60 arcmin footprint already drawn for the Orion Nebula.
deferred.vdb-5-vdb-34-vdb-36-vdb-99-vdb-104: Reflection light of nebulae already drawn: IC 59/IC 63 around gamma Cas, IC 405, the Witch Head around Rigel, Sh 2-1 and Sh 2-9.
deferred.vdb-88-vdb-95-vdb-154: Parallax errors comparable to the parallax (Hipparcos or Gaia); the nebulae cannot be placed.
deferred.vdb-93: Gaia EDR3 puts HD 53367 at 129 pc, but it is a member of CMa R1 at about 1 kpc; the parallax is not adopted.
deferred.vdb-48: 716 +/- 112 pc from a poor parallax of HD 37370; inside 2000 ly only at the 1-sigma edge.
deferred.abell-24-aro-121: Central-star parallaxes place them at about 720 and 940 pc.
deferred.fp-j1824-0319: Possible planetary nebula only, like FP J1912-0331.
deferred.ngc-6729: ESO/Uppsala lists 2.5 x 2 arcmin, below the 5-arcmin census limit; it sits just beside NGC 6726/6727.
deferred.ced-110-ced-111-ic-2631: Chamaeleon I nebulae: Cederblad and ESO/Uppsala give no size for Ced 110 and Ced 111, and Cederblad gives 2 arcmin for IC 2631.
deferred.ngc-1579-ngc-1999-ic-2087: Lynds (1965) lists 3 x 3, 2 x 2 and 4 x 4 arcmin, below the 5-arcmin census limit; the larger Cederblad sizes are not adopted over Lynds, as for NGC 1788.
deferred.ngc-1990: The parallax of Alnilam is poor (Hipparcos 1.65 +/- 0.45 mas), SIMBAD has no Collinder 70 parallax, and the SIMBAD nebula position is 30 arcmin from the star.
deferred.abell-74: Central-star parallax gives 658 +/- 37 pc, so distance minus error (620 pc) misses the limit.
deferred.abell-28: 4.47 arcmin SIMBAD-adopted diameter, below the 5-arcmin census limit (HASH lists 5.5 arcmin).
deferred.hdw-4-k-1-6: HASH radii give 2.9 and 3.3 arcmin diameters, below the 5-arcmin census limit.
deferred.hawe-5-tk-2-hdw-1: No angular size: neither SIMBAD nor Chornay & Walton (2021) list one. Also KPD 0311+4801, PN G134.3+02.5 and PN G093.1+05.3.
deferred.sh-2-129: The parallax of its ionizing star HD 202214 is too poor (Hipparcos 0.76 +/- 0.42 mas) to place it.
deferred.ngc-2626-vdbh-81: vdBH nebulae of at least 5 arcmin that miss the census: the star of NGC 2626, CD-40 4432, lies at about 926 pc (Gaia EDR3), and HD 153771 of vdBH 81 has an unusable parallax of 0.87 +/- 0.59 mas (Gaia DR2).
deferred.cederblad-foreground-stars: Cederblad names stars that are foreground to the nebula, so their parallaxes do not place it: gamma Cyg (IC 1318), Deneb (IC 5068, IC 5070, NGC 7000), Bellatrix (Ced 45), d Ori (IC 430), HD 35956 (Ced 47) and HD 168276 (IC 4706).
deferred.ced-106-ced-122-ced-145-ced-214: Listed only by Cederblad (1946) and not retained by Magakian (2003), so the nebulae are unconfirmed.
deferred.ced-125-dg-125-dg-141: Reflection light around b Sco, 2 Sco and HD 147702, inside or next to Sh 2-1 and Sh 2-9 already drawn.
deferred.mu-tau-hd-75649: Unnamed LBN patches tied to a star only by a positional match with Magakian (2003), not by a reflection-nebula catalogue.
deferred.antlia-snr: Supernova remnant candidate whose published distance estimates disagree widely; not yet settled.
deferred.gum-nebula: Whether the Gum Nebula is an old supernova remnant is disputed.
deferred.vela-junior: Published distances of RX J0852.0-4622 range from well within to beyond 2000 ly; not yet settled.

objects.name: Vela Supernova Remnant
objects.position_source: Green (2024), A catalogue of Galactic supernova remnants: G263.9−3.3

distance.source: VLBI parallax of the Vela pulsar, 3.5 ± 0.2 mas (287 +19/−17 pc); Dodson et al. 2003, ApJ 596, 1137

objects.notes: The nearest well-studied supernova remnant: a web of glowing filaments about 8 degrees across, left by a star that exploded about 11,000 years ago. The Vela pulsar it left behind spins 11 times a second.
objects.source_label: Sushch, Hnatyk & Neronov (2011)
objects.model_note: A sphere about 8 degrees across (radius about 20 pc at 287 pc) centered on the Green (2024) position. The filaments are illustrative: thin wavy arcs on the shell, red for hydrogen-alpha with teal [O III] sheaths just outside them. The all-sky H-alpha map cannot separate the remnant from the Gum Nebula behind it.

remnant.age_source: Vela pulsar spin-down age; Wikipedia: Vela Pulsar
remnant.drawn_as: Modeled red H-alpha and teal [O III] filaments

objects.name: Monogem Ring
objects.position_source: Galactic center (l, b) ≈ (203°, +12°) of the ROSAT X-ray ring; Plucinsky et al. 1996, ApJ 463, 224

distance.source: Plucinsky et al. 1996, ApJ 463, 224: Sedov-model energetics favor about 300 pc. PSR B0656+14, probably born in the same explosion, has a VLBI parallax distance of 288 +33/−27 pc (Brisken et al. 2003, ApJ 593, L89)

objects.notes: A huge, old supernova remnant about 25 degrees across in Gemini and Monoceros, found in 1971 by its soft X-ray glow. In 2026, deep images revealed faint hydrogen-alpha and [O III] filaments around most of its X-ray edge.
objects.source_label: Plucinsky et al. (1996)
objects.model_note: A sphere 25 degrees across (radius about 66 pc at 300 pc) around the X-ray center. The faint filaments are illustrative, after the 2026 hydrogen-alpha and [O III] images of Fesen et al. (arXiv:2608.26666), which trace them around most of the X-ray boundary; their exact positions are not modelled.

remnant.age_source: Plucinsky et al. 1996 (Sedov model at 300 pc); Knies et al. 2024, A&A 688, A90 (eROSITA)
remnant.drawn_as: Modeled faint red H-alpha and teal [O III] filaments

objects.name: Crab Nebula
objects.position_source: Origin of the Martin, Milisavljevic & Drissen (2021) 3D map, registered to their SITELLE deep frame; 1.9 arcsec from the Crab Pulsar

distance.source: VLBI parallax of the Crab Pulsar, 0.53 ± 0.06 mas (1.90 +0.22/−0.18 kpc); Lin et al. 2023, ApJ 952, arXiv:2306.01617

objects.illuminating_stars: The Crab Pulsar, whose wind powers the synchrotron glow
objects.notes: The remnant of the supernova seen from Earth in 1054: a cage of glowing filaments around a bluish glow powered by the Crab Pulsar, about 6,200 light-years away in Taurus.
objects.source_label: Martin, Milisavljevic & Drissen (2021)
objects.model_note: The filaments are measured in 3D: their sky positions and line-of-sight velocities come from the SITELLE map of Martin, Milisavljevic & Drissen (2021), and velocity becomes depth under uniform expansion. The brightest 0.045-pc cells of the hydrogen-alpha, [N II] and [S II] emission are drawn. The bluish synchrotron glow inside is modeled as a smooth ellipsoid, because the map traces only the filaments.

remnant.age_source: SN 1054, recorded by Chinese astronomers in July 1054
remnant.drawn_as: Measured 3D filaments (hydrogen-alpha, [N II] and [S II]) around a modeled synchrotron glow
